note: Draft v2, 21 Nov 2026. One change from v1, made after the v1 back test: a PASS from the score alone now needs at least one criterion that fails on cited evidence. A low score built only from missing evidence gives NEEDS HUMAN instead. Why: on v1, five funded memo companies were marked PASS with no flag (N1), each because short memos left most criteria unrated. Weights, criteria and thresholds are unchanged, so the rule was not fitted to the scores. Kushal approves only after reading the v2 back test.

rating_scale.label: Strong
rating_scale.meaning: Clear evidence, with at least one source outside the deck and form. Code blocks a Strong rating that rests only on founder claims.

rating_scale.label: Adequate
rating_scale.meaning: Evidence present, mostly from the deck or form.

rating_scale.label: Missing
rating_scale.meaning: The key fact is not there. Counts against the company.

rating_scale.label: Fails
rating_scale.meaning: Evidence shows it does not meet the criterion.

criteria.name: Stage fit
criteria.meaning: Truly pre-seed or seed. The round suits a first cheque of about $250K to $500K, and the fund could lead it (rounds under $1M) or commit early.
criteria.rate_4: Pre-seed or seed, raise under $1M, outside sources agree.
criteria.rate_0: Named Series A or later, or a raise far above what the fund leads.

criteria.name: Sector fit
criteria.meaning: Fits the fund's areas. The case names fintech, deeptech, consumer tech and consumer brands, but the fund publicly calls itself sector-agnostic. Founder behaviour matters more than the label.
criteria.rate_4: Clearly in a core area, and the founder's chosen label matches what the product is.
criteria.rate_0: Far outside, such as capital-heavy physical healthcare. Shown as a soft flag by default.

criteria.name: Not a regulatory bet
criteria.meaning: The business must not depend on the rules getting friendlier. A long but mapped regulatory path is acceptable when the founders have a milestone plan.
criteria.rate_4: No dependency on a rule change, or a clear, founder-owned path through the regulator.
criteria.rate_0: Only works if regulation becomes friendlier, with no plan if it does not.

criteria.name: No portfolio conflict
criteria.meaning: No overlap with a company the fund already backs. Checked against the full portfolio list. A conflict holds the application for Kushal.
criteria.rate_4: Clearly no overlap with any portfolio company.
criteria.rate_0: Direct overlap with a portfolio company.

criteria.name: Founder owns the hard part
criteria.meaning: The founder treats the core risk of the business as their own problem: credit risk in lending, density in delivery, the regulator in deeptech, retention in content.
criteria.rate_4: The founder names the core risk and a concrete plan they own, confirmed outside the deck or in a call.
criteria.rate_0: The founder says the core risk is someone else's problem.

criteria.name: Founder did the groundwork
criteria.meaning: The founders went to the customer first and did unscalable things: field visits, manual operations, pilots treated as learning.
criteria.rate_4: Specific, checkable groundwork with customers or the field.
criteria.rate_0: Built around an assumption with no contact with real customers.

criteria.name: Knows the numbers
criteria.meaning: The founder knows the numbers that matter for this business: repeat and cohorts for consumer brands, margin, acquisition cost by channel, retention. A missing number that the business should have drags the rating down. Revenue is not required for a pre-product company.
criteria.rate_4: Cohort or retention data, margin and acquisition cost by channel, consistent across deck and form.
criteria.rate_0: Numbers contradict each other, or volume is presented as revenue.

criteria.name: Path to market
criteria.meaning: A clear route to paying customers, and through any regulator. Rated apart from founder quality.
criteria.rate_4: Paying customers or signed pilots, and a concrete plan for any regulatory step.
criteria.rate_0: No customer, no route through the regulator, and no answer on who pays.

criteria.name: Capital fits the model
criteria.meaning: The business does not need far more capital than a pre-seed fund can give before it proves itself.
criteria.rate_4: Can reach the next milestone on this round.
criteria.rate_0: Only works with very large capital, such as dense dark stores or many physical sites.
sources: ePlane memo (cheque sized for a long path)

criteria.name: Defensibility
criteria.meaning: The company can survive a bigger, better-funded player copying it.
criteria.rate_4: A hard-to-copy edge, such as field execution, data or distribution.
criteria.rate_0: Easy to copy and the founder will not engage with the question.

criteria.name: Team covers the gaps
criteria.meaning: Someone owns operations, commercial and technology. A solo or one-sided team needs a plan to fill the gap.
criteria.rate_4: All three covered by named founders or leads.
criteria.rate_0: A critical gap with no plan, such as no one owning operations in a consumer brand.

weights_public._reading: The fund's public words: sector-agnostic, founders who go all in, very early, revenue not required.

weights_revealed._reading: What the memos show the fund actually backs: groundwork in the field, real repeat and margins, founders who own the risk.

thresholds._reading: Weighted average of ratings on the 0 to 4 scale. Starting values, tuned in the back test.

hard_flags.note: Recommendation cannot be GO. A person still decides.

partner_rules: A missing number drags the score. It is never skipped. (Meeting 1)
Score the evidence, not the pedigree. (Meeting 3)
Founder quality and path to market are rated separately. (Meeting 3)
Say which thesis lens was used and why. (Meeting 5)

findings.says: Pre-seed and seed. Often the first institutional cheque.
Most first cheques are pre-product and almost all are pre-revenue.
About $250K to $500K first cheque. Leads rounds under $1M.
Sector-agnostic in the fund's own words.
Reply to every form within 3 days, decision within about 10.

gaps.cost: Rubric is inferred from memos. Must pass the back test and Kushal's approval.
Conflict check can miss a clash. Kushal must confirm the list.
Stage check uses round size and cheque range only.

changes_from_previous: PASS needs a criterion rated 0 on evidence (thresholds.pass_needs_failure). Weights and thresholds unchanged.
